definitions.explanation: A climbing vine with cascading clusters of fragrant purple or white flowers. Wisteria is a beloved symbol of late spring in Japan.

examples.japanese: {藤|ふじ}の{花|はな}が{棚|たな}から{垂|た}れ{下|さ}がっている。
examples.english: Wisteria flowers are hanging down from the trellis.

examples.japanese: {藤|ふじ}の{香|かお}りが{漂|ただよ}っている。
examples.english: The fragrance of wisteria is drifting in the air.

examples.japanese: {藤棚|ふじだな}の{下|した}で{休憩|きゅうけい}した。
examples.english: I took a rest under the wisteria trellis.

notes:
{藤|ふじ} refers to wisteria.

Common expressions:
- {藤棚|ふじだな} (wisteria trellis/arbor)
- {藤|ふじ}{色|いろ} (light purple, wisteria color)
- {藤|ふじ}の{花|はな} (wisteria flowers)
- {藤|ふじ}{紫|むらさき} (wisteria purple)

Counter: {株|かぶ} (for the plant itself)

Cultural note:
Wisteria blooms in late April to early May. Famous wisteria viewing spots include Ashikaga Flower Park (Tochigi), Kawachi Wisteria Garden (Fukuoka), and Kasuga Taisha (Nara). The {藤|ふじ} family crest ({藤|ふじ}の{紋|もん}) was used by the powerful Fujiwara clan. {藤|ふじ} is also a common element in Japanese surnames like {藤田|ふじた}, {藤井|ふじい}, {佐藤|さとう}, etc.
